name: Pizza Marinara
steps: Mix flour and instant yeast in a large bowl. Add 300 ml of the water and mix until no dry flour remains. Dissolve 10 g salt in the remaining 20 ml water and knead it into the dough for 8–10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and leave at room temperature for 90–120 minutes until noticeably expanded.

Divide the dough into four equal balls, about 205 g each. Cover and rest 30–45 minutes so the dough relaxes. While it rests, crush the peeled tomatoes by hand and drain any very watery liquid; season with 3 g salt. Thinly slice the garlic. Do not cook the tomato topping.

Place a pizza stone or sturdy upside-down baking tray in the oven and preheat at its highest safe setting, ideally 250–275°C, for at least 30 minutes. On a lightly floured surface, press one ball outward from the centre to about 25 cm, leaving a raised 1–2 cm rim. Do not roll the rim flat. Work with one pizza at a time.

Spread one-quarter of the crushed tomatoes thinly over the centre, leaving the rim bare. Add one-quarter of the garlic slices, oregano and olive oil. Slide onto the hot stone or tray and bake for 7–10 minutes, or until the base is cooked and the rim is puffed with browned spots. Home ovens vary: bake longer if the crust remains pale or doughy. Repeat with the remaining three balls and toppings.
Serve each pizza hot as soon as it leaves the oven. The surface should show red tomato, garlic, oregano and olive oil, with no cheese; this is the classic marinara topping.
tips: The reviewed image shows a blistered raised crust and a cheese-free red tomato topping with thin garlic slices and oregano. Marinara pizza contains no seafood despite its name. Preheating the baking surface thoroughly is essential to cook the base before the tomato makes it soggy.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
